data.name: Rama
data.gender_notes: Rama is used as a male name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit root ram, 'to delight, to be pleasing'. Rāma means 'pleasing, delightful'. Its root is Sanskrit ram (रम्). Rama, the seventh avatar of Vishnu and hero of the Ramayana. Rama is a Sanskrit name meaning “Pleasing; delightful; charming”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Rama expresses “Pleasing; delightful; charming”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Sanskrit root ram, 'to delight, to be pleasing'. Rāma means 'pleasing, delightful'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rama total 15, reducing to 6. Number 6 is associated with responsibility, care and harmony.

vedic_reference.note: Rama is the seventh avatar of Vishnu, the preserver of the universe, and the central character of the Hindu epic Ramayana. He is considered an incarnation of God and an ideal man who embodies moral virtues. The name Rama is derived from the Sanskrit root 'ram', meaning 'to please' or 'to delight'. It is also a synonym for Lakshmana and Vishnu.

historical_references.reference: Rama, the seventh avatar of Vishnu and hero of the Ramayana.
